display.purpose: Product name and primary app identity.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: Quiet separation for cards, panels, summaries, and dialogs.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Use for the main action in a view or panel.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #0066cc; color: #ffffff; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 14px; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0052a3; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0052a3; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Use for secondary navigation and import/export actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #0066cc; border: 1px solid #d9d2c5; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 14px; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #e8f3ef; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0052a3; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Use only for destructive actions such as deleting a course.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: transparent; color: #a33b3b; border: 1px solid #d9d2c5; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 14px; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #f8ecec; color: #822e2e; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a33b3b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Paper Card
components.description: Shared container for course cards, panels, summaries, and dialogs.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #fffdf8; color: #1a252c; border: 1px solid #d9d2c5; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(28, 36, 48, 0.08); padding: 18px; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 10px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Full-width field for course and assignment data.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: #5c6776; font: 0.92rem/1.4 "Segoe UI", Tahoma, sans-serif; } .ds-field input { width: 100%; background: #ffffff; color: #1a252c; border: 1px solid #d9d2c5; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 10px; font: inherit; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0066cc; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #0066cc; }

narrative.overview:
CollegeGradez uses a quiet, practical desktop-tool language: warm off-white canvas, paper-like cards, and a single clear blue action color. The interface should feel dependable while a student is entering live academic information, with status and calculation results easy to scan rather than theatrically presented.

The visual system is intentionally restrained. Rounded containers, thin warm dividers, and a diffuse low shadow create separation without making the workspace feel heavy. Use the existing hierarchy and spacing rhythm to keep course editing useful at both wide and narrow window sizes.
keyCharacteristics: Warm canvas with near-white paper surfaces.
Blue primary actions and grade/GPA emphasis.
Segoe UI system typography with compact headings.
Thin beige borders and a single ambient shadow vocabulary.
Responsive layouts that stack secondary GPA and policy information below the primary editing content.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Keep blue as the dominant interactive and academic status signal. Do not introduce additional saturated accents for ordinary categories or decoration.

rules.name: The Clarity Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Reserve the largest or heaviest text for the product title and calculated results; supporting copy stays muted and compact.

rules.name: The Primary Work First Rule
rules.body: Keep the course editor and course list ahead of secondary GPA, policy, and explanatory panels when the layout stacks.

dos: Do use the established warm canvas, paper surfaces, beige borders, and blue action hierarchy.
Do keep calculated grades and GPA visually prominent but compact.
Do preserve the two-column desktop layout and stacked narrow-screen behavior.
Do make empty, invalid, error, and success states explicit with the established muted or soft feedback treatments.
Do use system typography and the existing radius/spacing scale.
donts: Don't add gradients, decorative illustrations, or high-intensity visual effects to ordinary editor surfaces.
Don't use the danger red for non-destructive status or primary actions.
Don't replace the paper-card hierarchy with dense dark surfaces or unbordered floating elements.
Don't hide secondary GPA or policy information above the primary course editing workflow on narrow screens.
Don't treat missing or invalid academic data as a successful numeric result.
